packet.headline_seed: Uber’s $14.8B Delivery Hero deal would nearly double its global footprint
packet.description_seed: Uber has agreed to acquire Delivery Hero in a $14.8 billion all-stock deal that would nearly double the company’s global footprint and create one of the world’s largest food delivery platforms outside China.

what: Uber’s $14.8B Delivery Hero deal would nearly double its global footprint

clean_source_blocks.text: BERLIN, July 16 (Reuters) - Uber agreed on Thursday to buy Germany's Delivery Hero at an equity value of $14.8 billion to create the largest food-delivery group outside China and stave off intensifying competition from U.S. and European rivals. The acquisition advances the U.S. ride-hailing firm's efforts to build a global food-delivery business that can better compete with Just Eat, owned by Dutch group Prosus, and U.S. rival DoorDash, which has been expanding aggressively. It is likely to face a complex regulatory process as the combination would create a platform spanning 99 countries with a combined pro-forma gross merchandise value (GMV) of $236 billion in 2025, according to a statement by Delivery Hero. "Together, we'll nearly double the number of markets where we offer both mobility and delivery services," Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said in the joint statement.

Uber Technologies is attempting to transform itself from the largest mobility platform into one of the world’s dominant logistics businesses, announcing a $14.8 billion offer to acquire Germany’s Delivery Hero in a deal that would dramatically expand its food delivery footprint while testing the limits of global antitrust regulators. Rather than simply adding restaurants and customers, the acquisition would extend Uber’s combined delivery and mobility operations to 99 markets worldwide, creating a network that generated approximately $236 billion in pro forma gross bookings during 2025, according to Uber. Uber is offering €41.50 per Delivery Hero share, implying an equity value of approximately $14.8 billion. Because Uber already owns roughly 24.8% of Delivery Hero directly and has additional economic exposure through equity derivatives, the effective purchase price falls to approximately $13.7 billion.

Prior to this acquisition proposal, Uber maintained an ownership position approaching 37% in Delivery Hero, incorporating derivative instruments. With Prosus agreeing to transfer its approximately 17% holding, Uber’s aggregate economic exposure will reach roughly 53%. The transaction represents a calculated effort to expand Uber Eats’ presence in territories where Delivery Hero has established significant market dominance. Delivery Hero’s portfolio encompasses Talabat throughout Middle Eastern nations, HungerStation serving Saudi Arabia, PedidosYa operating across Latin American countries, and Baemin dominating in South Korea. These represent geographic areas where Uber Eats maintains minimal or zero operational presence currently. Integrating these platforms would substantially amplify Uber’s international footprint within the food delivery sector. The strategic initiative emerges during a period when global food delivery operators are gravitating toward industry consolidation following extended periods of expensive market competition and substantial capital expenditure.

To ease those concerns, Delivery Hero will sell operations in 14 markets to U.S. investment firm SSW Partners for about €1.4 billion. Major shareholder Prosus has also agreed to sell its nearly 17% stake, leaving little room for a rival bid. Jefferies analysts, however, said the expected timing of the deal's completion signalled a "long slow march" ahead. "The use of a financial investor to get ahead of the antitrust questions could prove successful, though the long timeline to completion (2H27) suggests it won't be a straightforward review," the analysts wrote. Uber's bid was enabled in part by commitments Prosus made to the European Commission to secure approval for its acquisition of Just Eat Takeaway, which required the Dutch technology investor to cut its 26.5% stake in Delivery Hero, people familiar with the deal said. ---

[Lähde: AOL | URL: https://www.aol.com/articles/uber-launches-14-8-billion-062550000.html]
BERLIN, July 16 (Reuters) - Uber agreed on Thursday to buy Germany's Delivery Hero at an equity value of $14.8 billion to create the largest food-delivery group outside China and stave off intensifying competition from U.S. and European rivals.

The acquisition advances the U.S. ride-hailing firm's efforts to build a global food-delivery business that can better compete with Just Eat, owned by Dutch group Prosus, and U.S. rival DoorDash, which has been expanding aggressively.

It is likely to face a complex regulatory process as the combination would create a platform spanning 99 countries with a combined pro-forma gross merchandise value (GMV) of $236 billion in 2025, according to a statement by Delivery Hero.

"Together, we'll nearly double the number of markets where we offer both mobility and delivery services," Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said in the joint statement.

Uber, already Delivery Hero's top shareholder, has made the acquisition conditional on a minimum acceptance threshold of 50% plus one share.

The transaction, supported by Delivery Hero's management and supervisory board, is expected to be completed in the second half of next year.

The €41.50 per-share offer represents a roughly 34% premium to Delivery Hero's three-month volume-weighted average share price, it said. It was 9% above Wednesday's close, but nearer 40% above the "undisturbed" price before any deal talk started.

Shares of Delivery Hero were up 0.2% at 1436 GMT, while those of Uber rose 2%.

The deal would expand Uber Eats across Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Latin America, but is expected to face antitrust scrutiny due to overlapping operations.

To ease those concerns, Delivery Hero will sell operations in 14 markets to U.S. investment firm SSW Partners for about €1.4 billion. Major shareholder Prosus has also agreed to sell its nearly 17% stake, leaving little room for a rival bid.

Jefferies analysts, however, said the expected timing of the deal's completion signalled a "long slow march" ahead.

"The use of a financial investor to get ahead of the antitrust questions could prove successful, though the long timeline to completion (2H27) suggests it won't be a straightforward review," the analysts wrote.

Uber's bid was enabled in part by commitments Prosus made to the European Commission to secure approval for its acquisition of Just Eat Takeaway, which required the Dutch technology investor to cut its 26.5% stake in Delivery Hero, people familiar with the deal said.


---

The San Francisco-based transportation and delivery platform has initiated an official acquisition proposal for the Berlin-headquartered food delivery enterprise Delivery Hero, establishing a valuation benchmark of approximately $14.8 billion for the transaction.

The proposed consideration amounts to €41.50 for each outstanding share, delivered entirely in cash. This pricing reflects a notable premium above Delivery Hero’s current market valuation. The proposal includes a threshold requirement of securing acceptance from holders representing a minimum of 50% plus one additional share.

Uber stock (UBER) demonstrated positive momentum with a 0.82% increase following the disclosure. Delivery Hero (DHER) registered a modest 0.08% uptick.

The executive leadership and supervisory panel at Delivery Hero have provided unanimous endorsement for the proposed transaction. Officials have indicated their intention to advise shareholders to accept the offer, contingent upon their examination of the comprehensive offer documentation.

The transaction represents a calculated effort to expand Uber Eats’ presence in territories where Delivery Hero has established significant market dominance. Delivery Hero’s portfolio encompasses Talabat throughout Middle Eastern nations, HungerStation serving Saudi Arabia, PedidosYa operating across Latin American countries, and Baemin dominating in South Korea.

The strategic initiative emerges during a period when global food delivery operators are gravitating toward industry consolidation following extended periods of expensive market competition and substantial capital expenditure.

payload.title: Uber sopi Delivery Heron ostamisesta 14,8 miljardin dollarin kaupalla
payload.summary: Kauppa laajentaisi Uberin liikenne- ja toimituspalvelut 99 maahan, mutta järjestelyä odottaa pitkä kilpailuviranomaisten käsittely.
payload.content:
Uber on sopinut saksalaisen Delivery Heron ostamisesta kaupalla, jonka oman pääoman arvoksi on määritelty 14,8 miljardia dollaria. Järjestely loisi Kiinan ulkopuolelle maailman suurimman ruokalähetysryhmän ja kasvattaisi Uberin liikenne- ja toimituspalvelujen yhteisen markkina-alueen 99 maahan, mutta toteutuminen vaatii vielä vaativan viranomaiskäsittelyn.

## Kauppa laajentaisi Uberin uusille markkinoille

Yhdistyvän kokonaisuuden laskennallinen bruttotilausarvo olisi vuoden 2025 lukujen perusteella 236 miljardia dollaria. Uber arvioi lähes kaksinkertaistavansa niiden markkinoiden määrän, joilla se tarjoaa sekä liikkumis- että toimituspalveluja. Kauppa vahvistaisi Uber Eatsin asemaa etenkin alueilla, joilla sen oma toiminta on nyt vähäistä tai puuttuu kokonaan.

Delivery Heron palveluihin kuuluvat Lähi-idässä toimiva Talabat, Saudi-Arabian HungerStation, Latinalaisen Amerikan PedidosYa ja Etelä-Korean Baemin. Kauppa kasvattaisi Uberin kykyä kilpailla muun muassa DoorDashia ja Prosusin omistamaa Just Eatia vastaan aikana, jolloin ruokalähetysala on keskittymässä pitkän ja kalliin kilpailuvaiheen jälkeen.

Uber tarjoaa Delivery Heron osakkeista 41,50 euroa kappaleelta. Uber omistaa jo suoraan noin 24,8 prosenttia Delivery Herosta, minkä lisäksi sillä on johdannaisten kautta taloudellista altistusta yhtiöön. Näiden omistusten vuoksi kaupan tosiasialliseksi ostohinnaksi arvioidaan noin 13,7 miljardia dollaria.

## Viranomaiskäsittelyn arvioidaan kestävän pitkään

Kilpailuhuolten lieventämiseksi Delivery Hero myy toimintonsa 14 markkinalla yhdysvaltalaiselle SSW Partnersille noin 1,4 miljardilla eurolla. Prosus on puolestaan suostunut myymään lähes 17 prosentin omistuksensa, mikä pienentää kilpailevan tarjouksen mahdollisuutta.

Jefferiesin analyytikot pitävät pitkää toteutusaikataulua merkkinä vaikeasta prosessista. Kaupan odotetaan valmistuvan vasta vuoden 2027 jälkipuoliskolla, jos viranomaiset hyväksyvät sen. Analyytikoiden mukaan toimintojen myynti rahoitussijoittajalle voi auttaa kilpailuoikeudellisten kysymysten ratkaisemisessa, mutta pitkä aikataulu kertoo, ettei käsittely todennäköisesti ole suoraviivainen.

Toteutuessaan järjestely vahvistaisi Uberin asemaa maailmanlaajuisena logistiikka-alustana ja muuttaisi ruokalähetysmarkkinan kilpailuasetelmaa etenkin Lähi-idässä, Latinalaisessa Amerikassa ja Aasiassa.
summary_bullets: Delivery Heron oman pääoman arvoksi on kaupassa määritelty 14,8 miljardia dollaria.
Yhdistyvä palveluverkosto ulottuisi 99 maahan ja sen laskennallinen bruttotilausarvo olisi 236 miljardia dollaria.
Kaupan odotetaan valmistuvan vuoden 2027 jälkipuoliskolla viranomaiskäsittelyn jälkeen.

article.source_text:
BERLIN, July 16 (Reuters) - Uber agreed on Thursday to buy Germany's Delivery Hero at an equity value of $14.8 billion to create the largest food-delivery group outside China and stave off intensifying competition from U.S. and European rivals. The acquisition advances the U.S. ride-hailing firm's efforts to build a global food-delivery business that can better compete with Just Eat, owned by Dutch group Prosus, and U.S. rival DoorDash, which has been expanding aggressively. It is likely to face a complex regulatory process as the combination would create a platform spanning 99 countries with a combined pro-forma gross merchandise value (GMV) of $236 billion in 2025, according to a statement by Delivery Hero. "Together, we'll nearly double the number of markets where we offer both mobility and delivery services," Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said in the joint statement.

Uber Technologies is attempting to transform itself from the largest mobility platform into one of the world’s dominant logistics businesses, announcing a $14.8 billion offer to acquire Germany’s Delivery Hero in a deal that would dramatically expand its food delivery footprint while testing the limits of global antitrust regulators. Rather than simply adding restaurants and customers, the acquisition would extend Uber’s combined delivery and mobility operations to 99 markets worldwide, creating a network that generated approximately $236 billion in pro forma gross bookings during 2025, according to Uber. Uber is offering €41.50 per Delivery Hero share, implying an equity value of approximately $14.8 billion. Because Uber already owns roughly 24.8% of Delivery Hero directly and has additional economic exposure through equity derivatives, the effective purchase price falls to approximately $13.7 billion.

Prior to this acquisition proposal, Uber maintained an ownership position approaching 37% in Delivery Hero, incorporating derivative instruments. With Prosus agreeing to transfer its approximately 17% holding, Uber’s aggregate economic exposure will reach roughly 53%. The transaction represents a calculated effort to expand Uber Eats’ presence in territories where Delivery Hero has established significant market dominance. Delivery Hero’s portfolio encompasses Talabat throughout Middle Eastern nations, HungerStation serving Saudi Arabia, PedidosYa operating across Latin American countries, and Baemin dominating in South Korea. These represent geographic areas where Uber Eats maintains minimal or zero operational presence currently. Integrating these platforms would substantially amplify Uber’s international footprint within the food delivery sector. The strategic initiative emerges during a period when global food delivery operators are gravitating toward industry consolidation following extended periods of expensive market competition and substantial capital expenditure.

To ease those concerns, Delivery Hero will sell operations in 14 markets to U.S. investment firm SSW Partners for about €1.4 billion. Major shareholder Prosus has also agreed to sell its nearly 17% stake, leaving little room for a rival bid. Jefferies analysts, however, said the expected timing of the deal's completion signalled a "long slow march" ahead. "The use of a financial investor to get ahead of the antitrust questions could prove successful, though the long timeline to completion (2H27) suggests it won't be a straightforward review," the analysts wrote. Uber's bid was enabled in part by commitments Prosus made to the European Commission to secure approval for its acquisition of Just Eat Takeaway, which required the Dutch technology investor to cut its 26.5% stake in Delivery Hero, people familiar with the deal said. ---
